items.question: Where on the body must the practitioner perform ritual placement?
premises: Ritual placement targets specific body regions.
The belly and navel region are designated locations.
The phallus and secret part are also designated locations.
items.inference: The practitioner should place the ritual elements in the belly, navel region, phallus, and secret part.
items.plain_english: One should place it in the belly, in the navel region, in the phallus, and in the secret part.

items.question: What form should be meditated upon after completing the bodily placement?
premises: The bodily placement has been performed as described.
Meditation follows the placement.
The object of meditation is a bird whose nature is Śiva.
items.inference: After placing on the body in this way, one should meditate on a bird that is Śiva-natured.
items.plain_english: Having thus placed on the body, one should meditate on a bird whose nature is Śiva.

rows.grounds: ritual act of pleasing the deity

items.question: How must the deity be approached through external yoga before further rites?
premises: External yoga is the method employed.
The deity must be invoked.
The deity must be satisfied with effort.
items.inference: Through external yoga, one should invoke and diligently satisfy the deity.
items.plain_english: Having invoked the deity through external yoga and having satisfied him with effort,

items.question: What act completes the preliminary rite after satisfying the deity?
premises: Libations are offered after satisfying the deity.
The number of libations is one hundred.
Completion of this act constitutes the preliminary rite.
items.inference: Having offered one hundred libations, the preliminary rite is accomplished.
items.plain_english: Having offered a hundred libations, the preliminary rite is completed.

items.question: Who may perform desired rites and by what means after the preliminary rite?
premises: The preliminary rite has been completed.
Desired rites are to be performed.
The performer must be a knower of mantras using this mantra.
items.inference: The mantra-knower should perform the desired rites with this mantra.
items.plain_english: The knower of mantras should perform the desired rites with this mantra.

items.question: What practice causes a person to come under subjugation?
premises: The vital breaths are established.
The mantra is muttered one hundred and eight times.
If this is held, the target comes under control.
items.inference: Establishing the breaths and muttering one hundred and eight times brings the person under subjugation.
uncertainties: The referent of 'held' (dhṛtaṃ) is contextually ambiguous.
items.plain_english: Having established the vital breaths and muttered one hundred and eight times, if it is held, he comes under subjugation.

items.question: What do the subjugated persons continually provide to the practitioner?
premises: Those subjugated remain always under control.
They act according to each instruction.
They give desired objects and enjoyments.
items.inference: The subjugated always give the desired objects and enjoyments according to each instruction.
items.plain_english: Always subjugated, they give the desired objects and enjoyments according to each instruction.

items.question: How long does subjugation last when applied in matters of food and drink?
premises: The practice is applied in rules concerning food and eatables.
The subjugated person goes along with their lineage.
The effect lasts until death.
items.inference: When applied in matters of food and drink, the person and their lineage come under subjugation until death.
uncertainties: The exact parsing of sa+anvayāti as a single token is ambiguous.
items.plain_english: When applied in the rules of food and eatables, he goes under subjugation with his lineage until death.

items.question: What effect results from using a staff held by a man in this practice?
premises: A staff held by a man is used.
This practice is applied.
A woman becomes subjugated like the god of love.
items.inference: Using a staff held by a man causes a woman to become subjugated, inflamed like the god of love.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of manmathaḥ is metaphorically compressed.
items.plain_english: Or this staff held by a man makes a woman subjugated, like the god of love.

items.question: What duration and placement of casting brings a woman under control?
premises: The casting is performed for seven nights.
It is cast upon the head of the target woman.
The result is that she comes under control.
items.inference: If one casts upon a woman's head for seven nights, she comes under control.
items.plain_english: If one should cast upon whose head for seven nights, she becomes under control.

items.question: How enduring is the subjugation effect when the target is anointed?
premises: The target is anointed.
Subjugation occurs unfailingly.
The effect extends even to other births.
items.inference: When anointed, subjugation will unfailingly occur and persist even in other births.
items.plain_english: When anointed, subjugation will unfailingly occur, even in other births.

items.question: What social status does the foremost mantra practitioner attain in all the world?
premises: The practitioner holds or maintains the practice.
The context is all the world.
The foremost mantra practitioner becomes dear to all.
items.inference: The foremost mantra practitioner certainly becomes dear in all the world.
uncertainties: The object of dhārayati is implicit from context.
items.plain_english: Holding it, the foremost mantra practitioner certainly becomes dear in all the world.

items.question: What benefits arise from reciting the musalī mantra?
premises: The musalī mantra is recited.
Prosperity and fortune-bringing result.
Beloved persons are obtained.
items.inference: By reciting the musalī mantra, one becomes prosperous, fortune-bringing, and gains dear ones.
uncertainties: The internal structure of musalī+śa+mantra+jāpena is uncertain.
items.plain_english: By recitation of the musalī mantra, one becomes prosperous, fortune-bringing, and dear.

rows.grounds: compound: varaṇa + mūla + nāya (related to root)

items.question: How powerful is the effect of the varaṇa root among humans?
premises: The varaṇa root is applied likewise.
Its effect among humans is being emphasized.
The rhetorical question implies an extraordinary effect.
items.inference: Likewise, with the varaṇa root, what need is there to speak of its effect among humans?
uncertainties: The exact parsing and meaning of varaṇa+mūla+nāya is uncertain.
items.plain_english: Likewise indeed for the varaṇa root—what talk is there among humans?

items.question: How can an entire place be brought under subjugation through ritual gestures?
premises: Gestures beginning with añjali are used.
They are joined in proper order.
The entire place becomes subject to subjugation.
items.inference: By sequentially joining gestures beginning with añjali, one makes the entire place subject to subjugation.
items.plain_english: Having joined añjali and so on in order, one makes the entire place subject to subjugation.

items.question: What ritual procedure attracts the target woman using binding and mantra?
premises: The target woman is bound at the neck with a chain.
An attraction mantra is employed.
The mantra must be muttered.
items.inference: Having bound the target woman at the neck with a chain, one should mutter the attraction mantra.
uncertainties: Whether the binding is literal or symbolic is unclear.
items.plain_english: Having bound the target woman at the neck with a chain, one should mutter the attraction mantra.

items.question: What elements must be inserted at the end of the turīya-kukkuṭa mantra?
premises: The turīya-kukkuṭa mantra is being used.
The target's name is inserted.
The intended action is also inserted.
items.inference: At the end of the turīya-kukkuṭa, one should add the target's name and the intended action.
uncertainties: The exact identity of turīya-kukkuṭa is a technical term.
items.plain_english: At the end of the turīya-kukkuṭa, add the target's name and the action.

items.question: When should recitation begin to make a woman tormented by love?
premises: Recitation begins from a watch of the night.
The practice is performed in this manner.
The woman becomes tormented by love.
items.inference: Beginning from a watch of the night, one should mutter thus to make the woman tormented by love.
items.plain_english: Beginning from a watch of the night, one should mutter thus to make the woman tormented by love.

items.question: What physical signs manifest in the woman affected by the attraction rite?
premises: The attraction rite has taken effect.
Her secret parts and hips become sweaty.
Her garments and ornaments become loosened.
items.inference: The affected woman appears with sweaty secret parts and hips, and with loosened garments and ornaments.
items.plain_english: With sweaty secret parts and hips, and with loosened garments and ornaments,

items.question: What further signs of passion appear in the attracted woman?
premises: The woman is under the influence of the rite.
Her sighs are hot with the fire of love.
Her tender lips become dried.
items.inference: She breathes hot sighs from the fire of love and her tender lips become dried.
items.plain_english: With hot sighs from the fire of love and with dried tender lips,

items.question: How and when does the attracted woman come to the practitioner?
premises: The woman is fully affected by the rite.
She makes the añjali gesture.
She comes to his abode at night.
items.inference: With hands joined in añjali, she comes to his abode at night.
uncertainties: The exact sense of mukhena in this context is slightly ambiguous.
items.plain_english: With hands joined in añjali, she comes to his abode at night.

items.question: What extraordinary attraction can be achieved by heating with a lamp flame?
premises: An object is heated by oneself with a lamp flame.
The practice targets even celestial beings.
Urvaśī becomes subjugated and takes refuge.
items.inference: When heated by oneself with a lamp flame, even Urvaśī becomes subjugated and takes refuge.
uncertainties: The referent of taptaṃ and amūḥ is not explicitly stated.
items.plain_english: Heated by oneself with the fire of a lamp flame, even Urvaśī becomes subjugated and takes refuge.

items.question: From what distant realms can the desired woman be attracted by this practice?
premises: The practice has the power of attraction.
The desired woman can be drawn quickly.
Even worlds such as that of the nāgas are not beyond reach.
items.inference: Does it not quickly attract the desired woman, even from the world of nāgas and others?
uncertainties: The rhetorical force of na ākarṣati may imply affirmation.
items.plain_english: Does it not soon attract the desired woman, even from the world of nāgas and others?

items.question: How does a woman arrive when the rite is performed in fire?
premises: The rite is performed in fire.
The woman comes with fierce speed.
Her speed is compared to that of an intoxicated elephant.
items.inference: When performed in fire, the woman comes with a speed as fierce as that of an intoxicated elephant.
items.plain_english: And in the fire, the woman comes with a speed as fierce as that of an intoxicated elephant.
